comment: Curated list for repos.html. Categories and descriptions are hand-written; stars and activity are refreshed weekly by scripts/update_repos.py via GitHub Actions.

repos.desc: Free programming software for hundreds of radios. The CSVs on this site load straight into it.
Codeplug programming for DMR radios. The CHIRP of digital voice.
The rig-control library working behind most logging and digital-mode software.
Self-hosted web logbook, the actively developed successor to Cloudlog.
Fast desktop logger with rig control, maps, and cluster spots.
Scripted install of a whole ham software stack on a Raspberry Pi.
The LoRa mesh this site favors: routed through designated repeaters, with room servers for group chat.
The biggest LoRa mesh community. Flood-routed, huge hardware support.
Ham-licensed high-bandwidth IP mesh firmware for off-the-shelf WiFi gear.
A cryptographic network stack that runs over LoRa, packet radio, or any byte pipe.
Fast, clean, cross-platform SDR receiver. A great first stop for a new dongle.
The SDR swiss army knife: transmit and receive, dozens of demodulators.
The classic Linux and Mac SDR receiver, still going strong.
Decode weather satellites and a whole zoo of downlinks, pictures included.
Hundreds of simultaneous channels from one SDR, from Phil Karn KA9Q.
OpenWebRX+, a web SDR receiver your whole club can tune at once.
The software TNC behind most APRS igates and packet setups.
The software heart of most digital-voice hotspots.
Decode the 433 and 915 MHz chatter around you: weather stations, tire sensors, doorbells.
Track the aircraft over your house via ADS-B with a $30 dongle.
Real-time satellite tracking and pass prediction for working the birds.
